svg.text: The seven kinds of rock, cut in facets and lit from one side. Drawn by art/sheets/rocks.mjs from art/lib/rocks.mjs; nothing is traced or copied.
1. The seven kinds, now and after

Each kind as the game draws it today (redrawn here: one flat ink, its marks in the field's color) and as the uplift cuts it, at 22 px a unit, the size a laptop shows. A kind is told by its silhouette and its
Crystal: gems standing out of stone
Lodestone: long, banded poles, its field
Crystal: gems standing out of stone
Lodestone: long, banded poles, its field
2. One light, however a rock turns

Every kind and size at eight turns, 16 px a unit. The light stays at the upper left: a face brightens as it turns toward it and darkens as it turns away, so a spinning rock reads as a solid thing. Each rock
is one outline of six the game would hold for its kind and size.

A rock that takes more than one hit shows each it has taken as a crack more, in from its edge, the same cracks every time. The boulder holds five before its sixth breaks it; iron holds two when large and one
when medium; a large lodestone holds one.
Boulder, 0 to 5 hits held, 14 px a unit
Iron (large 0 to 2, medium 0 to 1) and lodestone (large 0 to 1), 22 px a unit

The same rocks at 6 px a unit, a small phone's, and at 10. Under 10 px a unit the fine marks are left out: rivets, glints, fractures, a lodestone's field. Silhouette, facets and a volatile rock's seams stay.

The rocks keep the game's own inks, a set for light palettes and one for dark, and take their lit and shaded tones from mixes with white and with the palette's field or text. Nothing new is added to a
6. Three ways to draw a rock, and why the plan cuts it

Flat, as now. Soft, a smooth blob with a crescent of shade. Cut, in facets. Each is shown at three turns. The soft rock's crescent has to be cut out of its outline again at every turn, which the game's

renderer has no cheap way to do; a rock baked with its shade on would carry its shadow round with it as it spins. A cut rock needs only one flat color a face, and a face's color follows from how it lies to
7. What the game gets of a rock

Left to right: its inks alone, which is the picture; its normal map, each face in the color of the way it points; the two together under the field's light; the same a quarter turn on; and with a blast going
off beside it, whose light the faces turned to it take. Every one is polygons in flat colors, which the game's renderer already draws.
